title: Intracardiac Perfusion and Brain Fixation for Immunohistochemistry
author: Daniel Manrique-Castano

steps.title: Prepare perfusion syringes
steps.instruction: Fill one syringe with 20 mL ice‑cooled PBS and a second syringe with 20 mL 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA); connect the PBS syringe to a winged infusion set.

steps.title: Anesthetize and expose heart
steps.instruction: Deeply anesthetize the animal until reflexes are absent and breathing is slow, then cut the thoracic cavity to expose the heart.

steps.title: Perform intracardial perfusion
steps.instruction: Puncture the ventral right ventricle with the winged infusion set, make a small opening in the left atrium, and perfuse 20 mL cold PBS (on ice) at a moderate constant speed; then switch the syringe and perfuse 20 mL cold 4 % PFA under the same conditions. Saline may replace PBS; monitor for pulmonary swelling or nasal outflow, which indicate improper vascular perfusion.

steps.title: Harvest brain
steps.instruction: After perfusion, remove the brain from the cranium and carefully strip the meninges to avoid tissue damage.

steps.title: Fix brain in PFA
steps.instruction: Place the brain in a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 12 mL 4 % PFA (volume ≥10 × brain volume) and incubate for 16 hours at 4 °C; ensure the brain is fully submerged to achieve ~1 mm/h penetration.

steps.title: Wash brain to remove PFA
steps.instruction: Wash the brain three times for 5 minutes each with agitation using 4 °C PBS or TBS to completely remove residual PFA.

substeps.instruction: Add cold PBS/TBS to the tube.
Discard wash solution and repeat two more cycles.

steps.title: Cryoprotect in 15 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Add 12 mL of 15 % (mass/volume) sucrose to the tube, keep at 4 °C until the brain sinks (typically 6–8 hours).

steps.title: Cryoprotect in 30 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Discard the 15 % sucrose, add 12 mL of 30 % (mass/volume) sucrose, and store at 4 °C until the brain sinks (generally 16–24 hours).

steps.title: Remove sucrose and air‑dry
steps.instruction: Discard the sucrose solution, extract the brain, roll it on clean absorbent tissue to remove residual sucrose, and air‑dry for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Freeze brain
steps.instruction: Place the brain on aluminum foil in a container with dry ice for 4 minutes, or alternatively wrap it in foil and submerge in liquid nitrogen for 8 seconds; avoid direct contact of the tissue with dry ice or liquid nitrogen.

substeps.instruction: Dry‑ice method: 4 min on foil above dry ice.
Liquid‑nitrogen method: 8 s immersion in LN₂ after foil wrapping.

steps.title: Prepare storage containers
steps.instruction: Label plastic or crystal containers for long‑term storage at –80 °C and pre‑cool the containers and forceps on dry ice.

steps.title: Store brain at –80 °C
steps.instruction: Using the dry‑ice‑cooled forceps, transfer the frozen brain into the pre‑cooled container and keep it at –80 °C for later processing.
